transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time listening to people when they are talking directly to me. It feels like my mind just drifts off even when I'm trying my best to pay attention, and it's starting to cause some real issues in my daily life.

Have you had this kind of trouble paying attention since childhood, such as in school, or did it start more recently? If it started recently, was it around a time when you were feeling very anxious or depressed?

Yes, I've actually had these attention difficulties since I was a kid in elementary school, well before I turned 12. It has been an ongoing issue since then, but it has become particularly troublesome over the last two years. It definitely didn't start recently, and I don't think it is linked to any anxiety or depression.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like at work or school, at home, and in conversations with friends or family? Can you give a brief example?

Yes, it definitely happens in multiple settings. In social and family situations, I often don't seem to listen when people are speaking directly to me, and at work or home, I have a really hard time organizing my daily tasks and activities.

Besides drifting off when people talk and trouble organizing tasks, do you also often lose things, forget appointments or chores, make careless mistakes, or avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort?

While I definitely struggle with listening and organizing my tasks, I don't really experience those other issues. I don't usually lose my things, forget chores, make careless mistakes, or avoid tasks that require a lot of mental effort.
Do you often have trouble sustaining attention on reading, meetings, or other longer tasks, or find yourself easily distracted by unrelated thoughts or things around you?
No, I wouldn't say I get easily distracted by my surroundings. I also don't particularly have trouble sustaining attention on things like reading or sitting through meetings.

When people are speaking to you, do you feel like you hear the words clearly but your mind drifts, or is it more that you have trouble processing or understanding what they said even though you were trying to listen?

It is definitely more like my mind just drifts away. I can hear the words clearly, but I often suddenly realize my attention has wandered elsewhere and I wasn't actually registering what was being said directly to me.
How much is this causing problems in your life—for example, has it led to mistakes at work, conflicts in relationships, or trouble managing daily responsibilities?

Yes, these issues cause notable problems in my daily life, especially because I have a lot of trouble organizing my tasks and managing daily responsibilities. Also, my difficulty with listening closely, combined with a tendency to blurt out answers before others finish speaking, often leads to misunderstandings and friction in my relationships.
Besides blurting out answers, do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble staying seated, talk excessively, or interrupt or intrude on others in conversations or activities?

Yes, I definitely get very fidgety and often find myself tapping my hands or feet or squirming in my seat. However, I don't really have trouble staying seated when I need to, nor would I say I talk excessively or interrupt others.
Before age 12, did you also often fidget, blurt out answers, or have other hyperactive or impulsive behaviors, or are those mainly more recent?
No, those behaviors aren't recent at all. I have definitely been fidgeting and blurting out answers since I was a young kid, well before the age of 12.

Onset before age 12, persistence across settings, and functional impairment are all confirmed, supporting ADHD combined presentation.
